Foreman run at 11:45: nothing was dead or hung, and I changed nothing.

**What's running**
- **CPU is the bottleneck:** 29 of the 32-core quota in use. The GPUs have spare capacity, but each run needs 3–4 CPU cores, so starting more runs wouldn't finish the batch sooner.
- **Memory:** 125.7 of 128 GiB used, but only 31.8 GiB is held by programs. The rest is file cache the system can free, so there's no out-of-memory risk. The out-of-memory kill count is still 2, as before.
- **GPUs:** My runs are on GPUs 1–4 (10 runs; 2 more run on CPU only). Other users hold GPU 0 (33 GiB), part of GPU 2 (17 GiB) and GPUs 5 and 6 (39.8 GiB each).
- **FEBio queue (old repo):** 42 waiting (physrot_p107–p149), 12 running, 1672 done. 54 finished in the last hour. The batch should finish around 12:35. The one failed job is an old one (zz_mc_c0.1_tied).
- **evo task queue:** empty. The 5 failed gate2 tasks from 10-28 are unchanged.

**Health**
- All 12 FEBio runs are using CPU and every log was updated within the last 31 s.
- p042, which was crawling last hour, has finished.
- All tmux services are up: biocage_sched, watchdog, gpusamp, preflight, evo_daemon and evo_keepalive.

**Needs a person**
- **Most physio_rot runs are failing:** 60 of the 95 finished runs ended in ERROR TERMINATION (it was 30 of 73 at 09:50). The owning role should decide whether the 42 waiting runs should still go ahead as they are. They will take about the next 45 minutes of the full CPU quota.
- **Disk is filling:** /raid has 365 GiB free and is losing about 49 GiB an hour. That's enough to finish this batch, but it needs archiving before the next one.
- **Failed evo tasks:** the 5 gate2 tasks still need their owning role.

I wrote a timestamp into `work/agents/foreman/last_run`. The daemon only reads that file's modification time, so the effect is just that the next foreman run is scheduled from 11:45.
